result:
Solution 2's answer, β_p = 3, is the one I judge correct. This rests on the lower bound and on rejecting the other two solutions, not on a full proof of the upper bound.

**Lower bound.** On a path with boundary values 0 and 1, every interior vertex has degree 2. The function g(x) = |x−a|^p + |x−b|^p is symmetric about (a+b)/2 and strictly convex, so the minimizer is always (a+b)/2, whatever p is. The dynamics is therefore identical to the p = 2 case, which is random Gauss–Seidel on the path Laplacian. That Laplacian has spectral gap of order n⁻², and each step touches one of about n vertices, so the convergence time is of order n³ log(1/ε). Hence β_p ≥ 3 for every p.

**Why Solution 1 fails.** Its complete-graph scaling n^{p/(p−1)} comes from the claim that one coordinate update reduces the error only by (ε/n)^{1/(p−1)}. That claim is not credible. A vertex jumps to the p-mean of its neighbors, which is a contraction toward h that does not degrade with the degree. The complete graph is fast, so max(3, p/(p−1)) is not the right exponent.

**Why Solution 3 fails.** It derives p+1 from a Polyak–Łojasiewicz argument that depends on a lossy Hölder step and on a Hessian bound that does not hold in general. Its claim that the path has condition number n^p contradicts the p-independence of the path dynamics shown above, which gives n³.

**Upper bound for p < 3.** I did not derive this myself. Solution 2's heuristic argument is only a sketch. The matching upper bound of n³ up to log factors for p < 3 is consistent with the path being the worst case in that range. It is also consistent with my recollection, which I could not check, that the exponent depends on p only for larger p.

CHOICE: 2
